role_instructions: Extract exact behavior, contracts, capabilities, states, authorities, consumers, GUI truth, failures, acceptance evidence, and consequential builder discretion from only this capsule. Identify underspecified obligations with exact source lines. Do not use external or prior-audit knowledge.

integrity_verification.source_sha256_recompute_reason: Recomputing the whole-document hash would require reading canonical content outside the permitted slice; the metadata value is reproduced without claiming independent whole-document verification.

observations.summary: Shortcut resolution is intended to be centralized around a defaults-plus-overrides KeyMap, consulted for application key events and rebuilt immediately after persisted edits.
Malformed or invalid shortcut configuration has a specified non-crashing fallback to defaults with a warning toast, and the edit/import path specifies duplicate validation.
The skills backend has explicit obligations for discovery, tool-reference validation, pre-launch readiness, compiled-context delivery, and on-demand retrieval.

Projection is a per-target interoperability layer distinct from PM-native runtime delivery; workspace ownership, provider ownership, target-specific manual override, and projection-failure independence are explicit.
Shortcut enhancements are required to support export/import, filtering, and binding discoverability, including distinct empty-query and no-match states.
Skills GUI capabilities include pattern permissions, combined filtering, on-demand preview, last-modified display, and per-skill validate-all results.
The stated readiness claim is readiness to draft a detailed implementation plan, while runner delivery still depends on platform specifications and may be stubbed pending that dependency.
Cleanup is designed as a pre-execution preparation and post-execution cleanup wrapper, with git-clean explicitly excluded from post-execution cleanup.

candidate_findings.title: Duplicate shortcut collision behavior is internally inconsistent
candidate_findings.description: One clause calls duplicate validation optional, later clauses require rejection, and the edit/import decision text still permits either rejection or stealing the binding. Implementers can produce incompatible user-visible outcomes while satisfying different portions of the window.

candidate_findings.title: Shortcut import version policy is not deterministic
candidate_findings.description: Missing or unsupported versions are described as rejectable but are also left open to best-effort parsing, while the later edge-case clause mandates only greater-than-supported rejection. Compatibility and failure behavior therefore remain non-uniform.

candidate_findings.title: Shortcut export payload is not fixed
candidate_findings.description: The export may contain override state or the fully resolved key map. Those representations have different reset, portability, and future-default behavior, especially when imported with Replace.

candidate_findings.title: Unknown shortcut action IDs have conflicting import requirements
candidate_findings.description: The primary import flow says all action IDs must exist, but the edge-case contract leaves skip-versus-reject to implementation. Atomicity and forward-compatibility behavior are therefore unspecified.

candidate_findings.title: The override-only model lacks an explicit unbound state
candidate_findings.description: Defaults are always merged with overrides and only overrides are stored, yet the GUI contract contemplates a user removing a binding. No tombstone, nullable override, or other representation distinguishes unbound from missing-and-use-default.

candidate_findings.title: Cross-platform modifier mapping and serialization authority are unresolved
candidate_findings.description: Modifier mapping may happen during config reads, writes, or display, while the stable wire representation may be either a string or structured object. This leaves round-trip identity and cross-platform sharing behavior implementation-dependent.

candidate_findings.title: Shortcut capture and event-consumption behavior remain open
candidate_findings.description: The window permits central or per-widget capture and leaves modifier-free shortcuts undecided. It also does not state whether a matched event is consumed before native text-widget handling, which can affect ordinary editing behavior.

candidate_findings.title: First-wins skill discovery lacks a closed search order
candidate_findings.description: First-wins makes path order authoritative, but the listed project/global and provider path order is illustrative rather than normative. Different builders can select different duplicate skills.

candidate_findings.title: Ask permission is configurable but its runnable behavior is deferred
candidate_findings.description: Readiness depends on permission state and runtime delivery applies a permission filter, but Ask is deferred to a later phase. The window does not fully define whether Ask blocks readiness, prompts during compilation, or permits launch pending an in-app decision.

candidate_findings.title: Skill create behavior for a pre-existing partial directory is unresolved
candidate_findings.description: The no-overwrite rule covers a directory containing SKILL.md, but a directory without SKILL.md may either fail or be completed. This changes recovery and accidental-file-preservation behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Concurrent skill edit protection is unresolved
candidate_findings.description: Overwrite-with-warning, conflict prompting, and locking are all left available. The resulting lost-update and user-interaction behavior is consequential and not fixed.

candidate_findings.title: Frontmatter-name mismatch remediation is not fixed
candidate_findings.description: The invariant that frontmatter name match the directory is explicit, but save may reject or offer a directory rename. The preference for rejection is not a mandatory contract.

candidate_findings.title: Validate-all presentation can violate its own full-table decision
candidate_findings.description: The decision and later acceptance require a full table for all discovered skills, yet the same decision row allows an errors-only modal for v1. Either implementation can be claimed conformant.

candidate_findings.title: Bulk permission persistence has two materially different models
candidate_findings.description: Bulk Apply may store one pattern entry or materialize explicit entries for every current match. Because explicit entries outrank patterns, the alternatives differ for future skills, later pattern changes, and reported affected counts.

candidate_findings.title: The skill-name validation regex is referenced but not defined
candidate_findings.description: Length and directory-match rules are stated, but the accepted character grammar is only called a regex. The assigned window cannot determine which names validate.

candidate_findings.title: Per-platform skill delivery remains unresolved
candidate_findings.description: The high-level registry, permission-filter, bundling, and skill-tool path is fixed, but path-versus-content and environment-versus-prompt transport still depend on platform specifications, and integration may be stubbed.

candidate_findings.title: Projection tracking lacks an exact state contract in this window
candidate_findings.description: Per-target projection and drift tracking are required, but target inventory, state values, drift calculation, persistence transitions, and repair failure transitions are not specified here.

candidate_findings.title: Clean-ignored can be configured but may never execute independently
candidate_findings.description: CleanupConfig and the helper both expose separate untracked and clean-ignored values, while preparation invokes the helper only when untracked is true. No behavior is specified for untracked false with clean-ignored true.

candidate_findings.title: Post-execution process termination receives an unexplained zero PID
candidate_findings.description: The cleanup function is specified to terminate a process, but the execution path calls it with literal zero after the runner returns. The window does not define zero as a safe sentinel or identify which process still requires termination.

candidate_findings.title: Cleanup-on-error and cancellation semantics are not guaranteed
candidate_findings.description: The wrapper is described as a sequence, but there is no explicit finally-style requirement for runner errors, cancellation, or panic. The additional rule to continue after preparation failure increases the importance of an exact post-run guarantee.

candidate_findings.title: Evidence-retention trigger and retain-last-runs semantics remain open
candidate_findings.description: The configuration includes prune_on_cleanup, but pruning must not run in cleanup_after_execution and may instead run manually or in the background. The definition of a retained run is also deferred.

candidate_findings.title: Skill import copy collision and rollback behavior are unspecified
candidate_findings.description: Import copies a folder into a selected discovery base, but the window does not state how destination collisions, partial copies, validation failure after copy, or rollback are handled.

candidate_findings.title: Compatible skill roots are not mapped to the GUI source filter
candidate_findings.description: Discovery includes compatible import roots, while list filtering exposes only Project and Global source categories. Provider, account-local, or other compatible roots lack a specified category.

candidate_findings.title: Validate all may omit shadowed duplicate files
candidate_findings.description: First-wins discovery allows later duplicate SKILL.md files to be skipped, while validate-all operates over discovered skills despite being titled as validation of all SKILL.md on disk. Invalid shadowed files may therefore escape validation.

candidate_findings.title: Sort persistence and preview representation remain implementation choices
candidate_findings.description: Sort preference may be session-only or persisted in GuiConfig, and preview may show body-only or the full file with collapsed frontmatter. These choices affect persistence and visible content but are not fixed.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Defaults-versus-overrides precedence and the principal KeyMap rebuild triggers are explicit.
Invalid shortcut configuration has an explicit non-crashing fallback, warning, and user toast.
Required tool-reference failures, optional tool-reference warnings, and exact failing-reference GUI reporting are distinguished.
Projection failure is explicitly not equivalent to PM-native runtime-delivery failure, and manual override is target-local.
Empty shortcut filter and non-empty no-match states have distinct required GUI truth.
Explicit per-skill permission entries have defined precedence over pattern entries.
Skill preview is load-on-demand and load failure must appear in the preview instead of silently omitting content.
Failure to read skill mtime must not exclude the skill from the list.
Validate-all must continue after an individual unreadable skill and report a per-skill error.
Post-execution cleanup is explicitly forbidden from invoking git clean; git cleaning belongs to preparation or the manual action.
Clearing agent output removes only directory contents and preserves the directory.
The readiness assertion is explicitly scoped to producing a detailed implementation plan rather than proving completed runtime implementation.

exact_evidence_refs.exact_quote: Merge defaults with overrides (overrides take precedence).
All key events (e.g. in composer, prompt fields) go through this map to resolve to `ShortcutAction` then execute the corresponding behavior.

On "Change", record new key combo, validate (no duplicate action binding; optional conflict check), update GuiConfig.shortcuts and persist; then rebuild key map so the new binding is active immediately.
**Key map rebuild:** (1) On app startup after loading GuiConfig; (2) After user saves a change on the Shortcuts screen (edit or reset); (3) After successful import (Replace or Merge).

If shortcuts section is missing, use empty overrides. If it fails to parse or is invalid, fall back to empty overrides, log warning, show toast "Shortcuts reset to defaults due to config error" (§7.11).
Use `validate_shortcut_binding` to reject duplicate action binding (same key bound to two actions); optionally warn on system shortcut.
discover skills from PM roots plus compatible import roots defined by the canonical skill system.
`required_tool_refs` problems block runnable `/readiness`, `optional_tool_refs` problems warn, and the Skills `GUI` surfaces the exact failing refs instead of flattening them into one generic error.

- compute runtime readiness before launch from validation state, permission state, and tool availability.
- bundle PM-selected skill content into the compiled context.
- expose the PM `skill` tool for on-demand skill retrieval during the run.

projection state and drift state must be tracked per target through `projection_targets` / `projection_targets[]`; target families may include workspace `AGENTS.md`, workspace `CLAUDE.md`, workspace `GEMINI.md`, workspace `.cursor/rules/pm-generated.mdc`, workspace `cursor/rules/pm-generated.mdc`, and provider/account-local `/account-local` config references where needed.

- workspace-owned projections are tracked separately from provider-root-owned runtime state; cleanup or repair flows must not confuse workspace-owned projected files with provider-root-owned account/runtime directories.
- editing a provider-native projection target directly requires switching only that target to `Manual Override`; repair acts on the chosen target and must not silently revert sibling targets.
- a projection failure does not mean PM-native skill runtime delivery failed.
Implementation plan should enumerate and wire key map in one central place (e.g. app-level key subscription) or per-widget; prefer central so behavior is consistent.
Key map must be consulted on every key event in focusable text areas. Slint: use a `FocusScope` (or window-level `key-pressed` handler) at the appropriate level (window or focused widget).
if user presses a key with no modifier, either reject with tooltip "Use a modifier (Ctrl/Alt/Cmd)" or allow (e.g. F-keys). Recommend: require at least one modifier for clarity.
use a format that is cross-platform and stable (e.g. string `"Ctrl+A"` or structured `{ "modifiers": ["ctrl"], "key": "A" }`).
"No duplicate action binding" is required.
either (a) **reject** with tooltip "Already used by <ActionName>" and do not save, or (b) **steal** (assign to new action and remove from old); implementation must decide.

On import, if `version` is missing or greater than the highest supported version, **reject** with message "Unsupported shortcut file version" (or "implementation must decide": skip unknown version and attempt to parse known fields for best-effort import).

**First-wins by search order.** Discovery walks paths in a defined order (e.g. project paths first, then global; within each, e.g. `.puppet-master/skills` then `.claude/skills` then `.agents/skills`).
Implementation must decide whether to treat "dir exists but no SKILL.md" as error or as partial state (e.g. offer to create SKILL.md only).

If the user has the skill open in the GUI editor and the file is changed on disk (e.g. by another editor or process), on save: (1) overwrite and warn "File was modified on disk; your version was saved", or (2) detect mtime/content change and prompt "File changed on disk. Reload / Overwrite / Cancel", or (3) lock file for v1 (complex).

**Decision:** Show a **full table** (all discovered skills) with a status column: OK or Error + message. This allows users to see which skills passed and which failed in one view. Summary line: "N OK, M errors." Optional: filter toggle "Show only errors" to collapse to errors-only. Implementation plan may choose errors-only modal for v1 if full table is deferred.
**Defer to later:** "Ask" means prompt user before an agent loads the skill.
**Explicit per-skill entry wins over pattern.**
"Import" means: user picks an existing folder containing `SKILL.md`; we copy that folder into a chosen discovery base (e.g. `.puppet-master/skills/<name>` or `~/.config/puppet-master/skills/<name>`).
(1) reject with validation error "Name must match folder name", or (2) offer "Rename folder" to rename dir to match (then save). Prefer (1) for v1 to avoid accidental renames.
MVP runtime delivery uses the canonical registry + permission filter + context bundling + `skill` tool path.
Serialize current overrides only (or full key map) to JSON.
Parse and validate: all action ids must exist, all bindings must be valid (no duplicate action binding; optional conflict check).
Unknown action id in file → skip or reject entire import; document to skip unknown and import known only, or reject with "Unknown action: X".

**Import would create duplicate binding** (same key for two actions): run `validate_shortcut_binding` after merge; if invalid, reject with "Conflict: key already used by <Action>" or apply and steal; implementation must decide (recommend reject).
on import, if version > supported, reject with "Unsupported shortcut file version."

As user types, filter the list: show only rows where the action label (e.g. "Move to start of current line") or the shortcut display string (e.g. "Ctrl+A") contains the filter text (case-insensitive substring). Empty filter = show all.
When filter is non-empty and no row matches, show empty list plus a single inline message (e.g. "No shortcuts match '...'") so the user distinguishes "no match" from "no shortcuts loaded."
If user removed the binding (e.g. no shortcut for that action), show only the action label with no "(...)" or show "No shortcut".
On confirm, update `GuiConfig.skill_permissions`: add or update pattern entry (e.g. `"doc-*": "allow"`) or set per-skill entries for each match.
If config persist fails after Apply, show error toast; do not update in-memory state as "saved" so user can retry.
Store last-chosen sort in session or in GuiConfig (e.g. `skills_list_sort: "name" | "source" | "permission"`) so it persists across opens.
(2) Source: All | Project only | Global only.

Selecting a skill in the list shows its body in a read-only pane (Skills tab); content is load-on-demand; user can copy text; "Edit" opens full editor. If load fails (missing file, invalid frontmatter), show error in pane instead of body.
Content = markdown body only (no frontmatter), or full file with frontmatter collapsed.
If mtime cannot be read for a path (e.g. permission denied), show empty or "--" in list; do not exclude skill from list.
all discovered skills are validated; results show in a full table (all skills) with status OK or Error + message; summary "N OK, M errors"; errors are copy-pasteable (selectable labels).
same rules as load_skill: frontmatter, name 1-64 chars and regex, name matches dir, description 1-1024 chars
If a skill path becomes unreadable during validate-all, show Error with message (e.g. "Could not read file"); do not abort entire run -- continue and report per-skill.
